answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks by requiring each identity to lock a time-bound stake before it may transact. A new agent starts with a small trust limit; as it completes verifiable work and earns attestations from peers, its limit rises like a tide lifting honest participants, while one proven misdeed slashes the stake. Spinning up thousands of fake identities then costs real capital per identity, and a shared reputation beacon lets the whole ocean of agents see which identities have burned stakes before, so attackers pay dearly for every fresh face while honest agents trade freely.
